faqs.q: Why does chimney flashing leak more than the rest of a Bloomfield roof?

runs.v: The chimney is the roof's largest penetration, and a Bloomfield chimney needs the apron, sidewall step, and upslope transitions all sealed, so a single failed counter flashing or cracked caulk joint admits water into the chase. Repairing chimney flashing means sealing that joint between the roof and chimney.

faqs.q: Is caulk a permanent fix for chimney flashing on a Bloomfield home?

runs.v: No. Caulk or roofing cement alone over no underlying metal is a temporary fix that cracks within a few years, per IIBEC; a permanent repair rebuilds the NRCA two-part system of step flashing and a counter flashing set into a reglet cut in the mortar joint.

faqs.q: Does a wide Bloomfield chimney need a cricket?

runs.v: Yes, if it is wider than 30 inches measured parallel to the ridge: the building code, at IRC Section R1003.20, requires a cricket, or saddle, on the upslope side. Many older Bloomfield chimneys built before this requirement lack one.

faqs.q: Does chimney flashing repair on a Bloomfield historic-district home need extra approval?

runs.v: It can. A property in a historic district can need extra review for exterior roofing work, separate from the construction permit, so confirm current requirements with the Bloomfield construction office before work begins. Per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private property owner.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for chimney flashing repair in Bloomfield, NJ?

runs.v: Usually not on a house: flashing repairs may not require a local building permit for minor work. A localized chimney flashing repair on a detached one- or two-family home counts as ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and needs no construction permit; on a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, repairing more than 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period requires one, so confirm with the Bloomfield construction office.
